Map pick by Flaming Fist.

Demos: [https://www.quakeworld.nu/w/images/7/72/Ff_vs_glx_dm3_pietro.qwz pietro (FF)]

"As the game started, Galaxy's players took the map quickly, aided by FF-Dag's unfortunate diss just a some 45 seconds into the game. They took a weak hold on RA and capitalized on the 4on3 situation. Dag got back in pretty quick and after about 5 minutes, FF got RL and held RA strong. They used it wisely and gained YA as well; of course this meant a lot of spawnfragging for FF and they made the scores even with GLX. FF controled Quad/YA/RA good, but still, GLX got in touch with RL/LG, so they got frags as well, but fewer. FF had to keep tight between YA and QUAD to manage this win. FF-Pietro got most of the quads, and he made an excellent job putting GLX away. Pietro also managed to twist the map, by taking some tremendous frags and taking the quad from GLX while they had the map." -Vortex === DM3-2 === FF: 217 - GLX: 90
[[Image:Ff-glx-dm3-2.jpg|320px]]
Map pick by Galaxy.

Demos: [https://www.quakeworld.nu/w/images/c/c7/Ff_vs_glx_akke_dm3_2.qwz aKKe (FF)]

"FF wanted this map too, so they got started. This round didn't start just as bad for them as the other round, but still abit unlucky for FF. But it didn't take long time for FF to get the map under control. They started to kill, with aKKe who got a bit carried away, and went up with a tremendous frag rate. While Gimp held YA safe and fragging like a maniac, Dag and Pietro helped aKKe with Quad. RA was safe as well, and this ment a lot of spawnfraggs for FF and they got the scores going from even to greater. Thought GLX trying to brake up YA and Quad all the time, FF held it safe. This round was a Good Game by FF, they held positions well, and GLX didn't stand a chance after the first 10mins."
-Vortex == Summary == * Score: 2-0 * Total frags ** FF: 362 ** GLX: 188 __NOTOC__ [[Category:Matchreports]]
